CODE
Art. 2.3.44.
Rewards due to the joint patrimony 
Each spouse is liable to pay a reward up to the amount of the sums he or she has taken from the joint patrimony to discharge a debt of his or her own and generally whenever he or she has derived a personal benefit from the joint patrimony.
A spouse who practises his profession within a company whose shares he owns owes a reward to the common patrimony for the net professional income which the common patrimony has not received and which he could reasonably have received if the profession had not been practised within that company.
 The common patrimony shall likewise be entitled to compensation for the loss it has suffered as a result of one of the acts listed in Article 2.3.36, where such loss has not been fully compensated by the annulment of the act or where such annulment has not been requested or obtained.
